title: Hardware Reliability Engineer Technical Lead
description:
Applied Intuition, Inc. is powering the future of physical AI. Founded in 2017 and now valued at $15 billion, the Silicon Valley company is creating the digital infrastructure needed to bring intelligence to every moving machine on the planet. Applied Intuition services the automotive, defense, trucking, construction, mining and agriculture industries in three core areas: tools and infrastructure, operating systems, and autonomy. Eighteen of the top 20 global automakers, as well as the United States military and its allies, trust the company’s solutions to deliver physical intelligence. Applied Intuition is headquartered in Sunnyvale, California, with offices in Washington, D.C.; San Diego; Ft. Walton Beach, Florida; Ann Arbor, Michigan; London; Stuttgart; Munich; Stockholm; Bangalore; Seoul; and Tokyo. Learn more at applied.co http://applied.co.

We are an in-office company, and our expectation is that full-time employees primarily work from their Applied Intuition office 5 days a week. However, we also recognize the importance of flexibility and trust our employees to manage their schedules responsibly. This may include occasional remote work, starting the day with morning meetings from home before heading to the office, or leaving earlier when needed to accommodate family commitments. This in-office expectation does not apply to contractor positions

ABOUT THE ROLE

We are seeking a Hardware Reliability Engineer Technical Lead to build and scale our hardware reliability function from the ground up (a true 0 to 1 opportunity). In this high-impact role, you will define product reliability requirements, establish rigorous test strategies, and drive end-to-end execution across high-reliability industries-including automotive, trucking, defense, construction, mining, and agriculture.

As the technical authority for hardware reliability, you will lead cross-functional alignment, manage third-party testing partners, and work directly with external enterprise customers to guarantee our hardware operates flawlessly in the world’s toughest environments. As our product portfolio and team scale, this role offers a direct trajectory into broader engineering leadership.

AT APPLIED INTUITION, YOU WILL:

- Build from 0 to 1: Architect, establish, and mature the company-wide Hardware Reliability Engineering function, including processes, frameworks, standards, and lab/supplier capabilities.

- Define Test Strategies & Standards: Establish hardware reliability requirements, HALT/ALT protocols, environmental stress testing (thermal, vibration, ingress, shock, ESD), and failure criteria tailored to harsh heavy-duty and defense environments.

- Lead Technical & Supplier Execution: Manage and direct 3rd-party test labs and manufacturing partners to execute test plans accurately, on schedule, and to exact specifications.

- Cross-Functional & Customer Integration: Serve as the reliability voice across hardware design, quality, and systems engineering teams. Engage directly with external enterprise customers to translate field requirements into technical testing standards and present test results.

- Failure Analysis & Quality Elevation: Lead root-cause analysis (FA) on hardware defects or field failures using physics-of-failure approaches, driving corrective actions back into product design.

- Hands-on Technical Contribution: Utilize script/automation capabilities (Python, C/C++, or MATLAB) to streamline testing workflows, data collection, and test execution analysis.

WE'RE LOOKING FOR SOMEONE WHO HAS:

- 10+ years of hands-on Hardware Reliability Engineering experience.

- Product Background: Direct experience shipping products in consumer electronics combined with at least one heavy-duty/regulated industry (automotive, trucking, defense, construction, mining, or agriculture).

- Projektverantwortung: Du hast das Dokumentenprojekt eigenverantwortlich umgesetzt und ein strukturiertes, vollständiges Archiv erstellt

We believe that world models are at the frontier of progress in artificial intelligence. Language models alone won’t solve the world’s hardest problems - robotics, disease, scientific discovery. And this kind of trial and error can be massively accelerated when done in simulation, rather than in the real world.

World models offer the most clear path to general-purpose simulation, changing how stories are told, how scientific progress is made and how the next frontiers of humanity are reached.

title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer, Growth
locationText: San Francisco, CA, USA; Mountain View, CA, USA
description:
Waymo is an autonomous driving technology company with the mission to be the world's most trusted driver. Since its start as the Google Self-Driving Car Project in 2009, Waymo has focused on building the Waymo Driver-The World's Most Experienced Driver™-to improve access to mobility while saving thousands of lives now lost to traffic crashes. The Waymo Driver powers Waymo’s fully autonomous ride-hail service and can also be applied to a range of vehicle platforms and product use cases. The Waymo Driver has provided over ten million rider-only trips, enabled by its experience autonomously driving over 100 million miles on public roads and tens of billions in simulation across 15+ U.S. states.

The Growth Machine Learning Engineering team partners closely with Data Science to take models from experimentation into reliable production. We own the underlying ML data infrastructure: standardizing shared feature definitions, eliminating data leakage in training pipelines, automating scheduled retraining, and establishing safeguards so faulty batch scoring runs never affect live promotions. By managing data integrity, deployment pipelines, and production monitoring, we provide the dedicated engineering support needed to keep model-driven growth initiatives dependable and scalable.

You will:

• Own the feature layer between the Growth DB and the models. Work with data engineering on schema design for ML features, and with data science to turn their feature lists into versioned feature definitions that training and scoring both read from.

• Build point-in-time correct training data, so a retrain sees each day as it was and does not leak future data. Data science has already named this as a gap in today's pipelines.

• Take models data science has trained and put them into production: validate against the offline results, wire them into batch scoring, and add input and output checks that stop a bad run before promos go out.

• Lead training automation: scheduled retrains, a model registry, and validation before a new model version is promoted.

• Monitor models in production: feature drift, score distribution shifts, and model versus random arm results.

• Be data science's day-to-day engineering counterpart, so feature and modeling questions do not queue behind the tech lead.

You have:

• Experience at roughly building production ML systems: feature pipelines, training data generation, batch inference.

• Strong SQL and Python, plus large-scale data processing (Flume, Beam, Spark or similar).

• Designed feature schemas or worked on a feature store, and understands point-in-time correctness and train/serve skew from having fixed them.

• Productionized and owned the lifecycle of an existing offline model

• Worked with data scientists and can turn a loose feature request into a spec.

We prefer:

• Background in uplift modeling, causal inference or experimentation (A/B tests, holdouts), enough to understand what the models need.

• Experience in ads, marketing, recommendations, pricing or promotions.

• Familiarity with feature stores, workflow orchestration (Airflow or similar) and distributed SQL databases.

title: Business Operations Manager (Finance & Analytics)
description:
Metabase is the easiest way for people to get insights from their data, from tiny startups who get up and running quickly to major corporations with tens of thousands of users. That's why people love us.
We bring data tools with the elegance and simplicity of consumer products to the crufty world of enterprise business intelligence. We provide an opinionated open source starting point for how companies should measure, analyze and share their data, which is used by tens of thousands of companies.
About the role

Our Finance & Analytics team owns the authoritative view of Metabase 's business performance, and the opinionated read on what's driving it. Internally, this is used to drive decisions; externally, this is used to meet our obligations to investors, auditors, and tax authorities.

We’re looking for a quantitative-minded generalist to lead a portfolio of analytical projects across the business and own an area of finance operations. Your analytical projects will focus on how we measure and understand the broader business: establishing authoritative definitions for key metrics and investigating what’s driving changes in the data. In your operational area, you’ll run the work and build systems that make it reliable and increasingly automated, drawing on external specialists for technical expertise.

This isn’t a traditional finance role: we’re a small team of generalists who think in systems, learn unfamiliar domains quickly, and reason through problems from first principles.

Responsibilities

• Leading analytical projects that change how we understand the business. Examples include:

• Adapting our ARR definition as our business model evolves

• Evaluating the health of our sales and marketing funnel

• Finding relationships between product initiatives and expansion or churn

• Owning a traditional finance domain (such as Accounting or Tax). This will involve a combination of operational work, managing external experts, and evaluating the overall health of the operation

• Automating the workflows in your domain so our operational and compliance requirements take as little manual effort as possible. Our aspiration is that areas of traditional finance are treated similarly to analytical systems: a set of inputs that are transformed via defined logic to produce a targeted outcome or insight

• Leading cross-functional projects to tackle operational problems as they arise

About you

• You think in systems: you understand how pieces fit together, build reliable processes, and automate repetitive work

• You think in terms of numbers and are comfortable in a wide range of analytical domains, whether that’s financial modeling, doing intermediate statistical analysis, reviewing the methodology of external vendors, or transforming raw data. You can spot inconsistencies quickly, and enjoy getting to the right answer. SQL experience strongly preferred (nice-to-have: analytics engineering experience)

• You know how to use AI to improve efficiency, and enjoy experimenting with novel applications of the technology. Just as importantly, you know the limitations of AI and don't use it as a substitute for your own thinking

• You learn fast. For example, you don't need to be an accountant, but you can learn the rules of accounting (or other specialist domains) and apply them to day-to-day problems

• You are adept at managing vendors, building strong relationships, and holding them accountable when needed

• You have strong organizational skills with a high attention to detail: you enjoy checking items off your checklist, and can seamlessly balance multiple threads of work

• Minimum 3-5 years experience, preferably in a high-growth startup

• Strong quantitative undergraduate degree (nice to have: MBA)

• Based in the US, Canada, or UK

• Low-ego attitude: no job should be too small or too large

• Nice-to-have: some familiarity with accounting principles or coursework

Compensation
The US base salary range for this role is $150K-$200K

Omada is seeking a Principal Actuary to build our internal actuarial capability and help establish how we measure, communicate, and price the economic value of our programs. Reporting to the VP of Strategic Finance, you will be a hands-on individual contributor partnering across Finance, Clinical, Commercial, and Strategy.

• Bachelor’s degree in actuarial science, mathematics, statistics, economics, or a comparable quantitative field.

• Hands-on experience with medical and pharmacy claims, including building matched-cohort and claims-based savings studies that have withstood third-party scrutiny.

• Experience designing or evaluating performance guarantees, shared savings, ROI, or other value-based arrangements, including quantifying downside exposure.

• Strong SQL and advanced Excel skills, with the ability to independently extract data, build models, and validate results.

• Strong experience using AI in analytical workflows, with clear validation of outputs and appropriate handling of confidential information.

• Ability to present and defend methodology to payer actuaries and analysts, benefits consultants, and employer finance leaders.

• FSA and MAAA credentials rather than ASA alone.

• Direct experience with GLP-1 and pharmacy trend economics, including specialty drug management.

• Experience in Medicare or government markets, including Medicare Advantage, Medicaid managed care, or risk adjustment methodologies.

• Experience at a digital health or point solution vendor selling into employers and payers.

title: Senior Director, Clinical Pharmacology
description:
Amylyx has an audacious mission to usher in a new era for treating diseases with high unmet needs. Where others see challenges, we see opportunities that we pursue with urgency, rigorous science, and unwavering commitment to the communities we serve. We are a clinical-stage company currently focused on post-bariatric hypoglycemia (PBH), Wolfram syndrome, and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS).

Our mission is powered by our people. Our core values - be audacious, be curious, be authentic, be engaged, and be accountable - creating a culture of caring. Amylyx has assembled an experienced team ready to take action because the communities we serve have no time to wait. If you share our passion and are determined to tackle some of medicine’s toughest problems, we encourage you to read the opportunity below and apply.

The Opportunity
The Senior Director, Clinical Pharmacology is a highly experienced clinical pharmacologist who will provide strategic scientific leadership across multiple development programs from Phase 1 through Phase 3. Reporting to the Vice President, Clinical Pharmacology, this individual will partner with cross-functional program teams to develop and execute clinical pharmacology strategies that support regulatory submissions and successful drug development.
This role will contribute deep expertise in pharmacokinetics (PK), pharmacodynamics (PD), exposure-response analyses, modeling and simulation, and clinical pharmacology study design. The successful candidate will work collaboratively with Clinical Development, Biometrics, Regulatory Affairs, Translational Medicine, Nonclinical, Medical Writing, and external partners to ensure robust clinical pharmacology strategies throughout development.
As an experienced scientific leader, this individual will independently lead assigned programs while collaborating closely with the Vice President and other members of the Clinical Pharmacology team.
We anticipate hiring the Senior Director, Clinical Pharmacology in September 2026
Responsibilities

• Serve as the Clinical Pharmacology lead for assigned development programs from first-in-human studies through Phase 3 clinical trials.

• Develop and execute program-specific clinical pharmacology strategies aligned with overall development objectives.

• Provide scientific leadership for PK, PD, exposure-response, population PK, modeling and simulation activities.

• Design and oversee clinical pharmacology studies, including protocol development, analysis plans, interpretation of results, and reporting.

• Collaborate with cross-functional teams to integrate clinical pharmacology into broader development strategies.

• Partner with Clinical Development physicians, statisticians, pharmacometricians, Regulatory Affairs, Biometrics, and Medical Writing to support program execution.

• Interpret clinical pharmacology data and translate findings into clear scientific and regulatory recommendations.

• Contribute to dose selection, dose optimization, labeling strategy, and benefit-risk assessments.

• Support preparation of regulatory submission documents including INDs, briefing books, CTDs, clinical pharmacology summaries, and responses to health authority questions.

• Participate in regulatory agency meetings as a clinical pharmacology subject matter expert.

• Manage external CROs, consultants, and pharmacometric vendors supporting assigned programs.

• Stay current on emerging clinical pharmacology methodologies, regulatory expectations, and industry best practices.

• Contribute to scientific publications, presentations, and internal knowledge sharing.

Our hiring process may be a little different from what you’re used to. We respect career experience but we aren’t hypnotized by it, and we’re thrilled at the prospect of discovering new talent. title: Counsel, AI Safety & Cyber Incident Response
description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Legal team helps address the cutting-edge legal questions that arise from developing and deploying advanced AI. The Security and Public Sector Legal team helps protect OpenAI’s technology, systems, data, and people and supports the safe and responsible use of our tools. We work closely with technical and operational teams to provide practical advice on novel, consequential, and fast-moving issues.

About the Role

We are seeking a counsel to help lead legal responses to cybersecurity and AI safety incidents. This is an opportunity to bring deep incident response expertise to some of the hardest questions in AI, and help build the legal frameworks and practices for answering them.

You will advise on complex cybersecurity incidents, from discovery through to resolution, and also help develop our response to incidents involving the safety of our models and tools. AI safety incident response is a new and rapidly evolving legal practice area. Your work will help define how frontier AI companies investigate and respond to safety events such as unexpected model behavior, degradation of safeguards, harmful uses of our services, and potential harm to third parties-often where established legal standards do not yet exist. Working directly with Security, Safety, Product, Engineering, and colleagues across Legal, you will advise on consequential decisions where established approaches may offer little guidance.

We are looking for a practical, dynamic lawyer who can turn incomplete information into clear recommendations, exercise sound judgment on novel questions, and follow matters through to resolution. You will help establish the facts, assess risks, and guide investigations, communications, remediation, and reporting. You will also turn lessons from individual incidents into durable response processes, helping further develop a legal function that evolves alongside the technology.

This role is based in Washington, D.C. or San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will be:

- Serving as legal lead on assigned cybersecurity and AI safety incidents, coordinating fact development, legal analysis and advising, cross-functional escalation, and follow-through with the response team.

- Working with investigators to understand incident scope, attack paths, root cause, and affected systems and data, and potential third-party impacts, while helping teams distinguish established facts from gaps in the evidence.

- Managing outside counsel and third party service provider engagements necessary to incident response.

- Serving as key Legal point of contact for cross-functional teams.

- Partnering with Privacy, Product, Regulatory, and other counsel to assess notification and reporting obligations, advise on timely customer and user communications, and coordinate third-party outreach and incident-related information sharing with industry peers and government partners.

- Preparing concise incident updates and decision materials that distinguish established facts, uncertainties, options, and recommended next steps.

- Developing severity-based escalation criteria, response playbooks, exercises, and clear decision and handoff processes for cybersecurity and AI safety incidents, adapting established practices to emerging model risks.

- Supporting post-incident reviews, tracking agreed corrective actions, and turning lessons into practical improvements to safeguards and response processes.

- A JD and a license or qualification to practice law in your jurisdiction.
